lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Owned the credit reviews for the small-business loan book and the watch list the lending officers used.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; the findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Wrote the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuaton, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Check that the LinkedIn URL works.
Check that the email and phone number are ones you actively monitor.
Remove the date of birth and nationality for most US job applications.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary and can introduce bias.

items.says: Specify how the 40% close-efficiency improvement was measured.
Clarify your contribution to decisions beyond standardizing the capital-plan template.
items.because: The bullet currently stops at process.

items.says: Describe the significance of the board-pack commentary or the decisions it supported.
items.because: Explaining lines more than 5% off budget reads primarily as a task.

items.says: Correct the mismatch between free cash flow to equity and WACC.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity is ordinarily discounted at the cost of equity, not WACC.

items.says: Recalculate the group EBITDA margin rather than adding business-unit margins.
items.because: A group margin needs to use consolidated EBITDA and revenue, with relevant eliminations.

items.says: Verify that the forecast error and USD 40M debt repayment are documented.
Distinguish the forecast’s contribution to the debt-repayment decision from sole causation.
Add the scope of the credit reviews and watch list, such as portfolio size or review volume.
Check that the approval-rate comparison uses comparable periods.
Check that “no rise in early defaults” has an adequate observation window.
State the period used for the before-and-after covenant-test figures consistently.
items.because: That makes the reduction easier to trust.

items.says: Clarify whether 6 to 3 hours covers total memo preparation or just spreading, and whether it is typical or measured.
Do not treat proximity to market price as proof the valuation was accurate.
Make the valuation date, market-price comparison, and independent assumptions clear in the underlying project.
Specify the direction of the discount-rate change and whether “1-point” means one percentage point.
items.because: Readers should be able to reconcile the USD 52 and USD 44 values.

items.says: Identify which spring pitch the investment club used the model in.
items.because: The project dates may make that unclear.

items.says: Verify that the fund had an FP&A team and that the bullet describes your role.
items.because: It does not fit naturally with the other fund bullets.

items.says: Add a measurable benefit to the performance-report bullet if one exists.
Remove the cash-forecast bullet from the student-fund section unless it was a separate project.
items.because: It closely duplicates the Stonebridge forecast and is implausibly placed in a 2018–19 student-fund role.

items.says: Correct the typo in “valuaton.”
Keep only methods you can confidently explain.
Be ready to account for the period after Stonebridge ended in June 2025.
items.because: The résumé need not explain every gap, but the dates should be accurate.
